objectives.text: Given the functional characteristics of an AC power source and the intended load, DESCRIBE the necessary components and the wiring scheme to provide a safe Electrical Distribution System.

enabling.text: EXPLAIN the following terms as they apply to Electrical Distribution Systems:
DESCRIBE the protection provided by each of the following:
STATE the purpose of circuit breakers.
Given a simple schematic of a circuit breaker control circuit, DESCRIBE the operation of that breaker during remote operation and automatic tripping.
LIST the three most widely-used protective features that may be incorporated into a circuit breaker control circuit.
STATE the function of motor controllers.
STATE three protective features (overloads) that may be incorporated into a motor controller.
Given a simplified drawing of a motor controller, DESCRIBE the operation of that motor controller.
DEFINE the following terms as they apply to wiring schemes used in power distribution systems:
DESCRIBE the two methods of connecting single-phase loads to a three-phase power source.
DESCRIBE the purpose of the following power distribution schemes.

Bond - the permanent joining of metallic parts or circuits assuring electrical continuity and capacity to safely conduct any current likely to be imposed.

Leg - a current-carrying conductor intended to deliver power to or from a load normally at an electrical potential other than ground.

body.text: If a breaker opens on a short circuit or overload, the handle goes to the trip-free position, midway between ON and OFF.
A bimetallic thermal trip element has an inverse-time characteristic. An extremely high current trips the breaker very rapidly.
For moderate overload currents, it operates more slowly.
An arc chute divides the arc into small segments and quenches it.
Remote operation needs a control circuit. Control power is supplied by an AC source and rectified to DC.

body.text: This includes starting and stopping the motor, and protecting it from overcurrent, undervoltage, and overheating.
The two basic categories are the manual controller and the magnetic controller.
When power fails, the manual controller contacts remain closed, and the motor restarts when power is restored.
A magnetic controller automatically performs all operations in the proper sequence after the closure of a master switch.
Overload devices protect the motor from overcurrent. Those commonly used are:
An LVP controller de-energizes the motor in a low voltage condition and keeps it from re-starting automatically.

body.alt: LVP controller circuit with START and STOP buttons, contactor coil M, contact Ma, and overloads on the motor lines.

body.text: Pushing START energizes coil M and closes the M and Ma contacts. The Ma contact keeps the circuit complete when the button is released.
On low voltage, the M coil drops out and the contacts open. START must then be pushed to restart the motor.
An LVR controller de-energizes the motor in a low voltage condition and restarts it when normal voltage is restored.

examples.title: Closing a breaker remotely
examples.problem: Follow the control circuit when the control switch is turned to close.
steps: The switch completes a path through the closing relay (CR).
The closing relay shuts an auxiliary contact, which energizes the closing coil (CC).
The closing coil shuts the breaker, which latches closed.
The "b" contact opens, de-energizing the closing relay and closing coil.
The "a" contact closes, enabling the trip circuit.
examples.answer: The breaker is closed and the trip circuit is enabled

examples.title: LVP controller on low voltage
examples.problem: A motor on an LVP controller sees a low voltage condition. What happens?
steps: The M coil drops out at a pre-determined voltage.
The M and Ma contacts open.
Normal voltage returns, but the Ma contact stays open.
examples.answer: The START button must be pushed to restart the motor

facts.q: What is the difference between an LVP and an LVR controller?
facts.a: Both de-energize the motor on low voltage. An LVP keeps it from restarting automatically, and an LVR restarts it when normal voltage is restored.

facts.q: What must be done before operating a disconnect?
facts.a: Open the breaker first. Never operate a disconnect under load.

facts.q: How is a breaker in the TRIP FREE position reset?
facts.a: It must be positioned to the OPEN position first.

facts.q: What protects a circuit from an overcurrent condition only?
What is a leg in a power distribution system?
facts.a: A current-carrying conductor intended to deliver power to or from a load, normally at an electrical potential other than ground.

summary.text: Protective relays cause prompt removal of any part of a power system that might cause damage.
The three most commonly-used automatic trip features for a circuit breaker are overcurrent, underfrequency, and undervoltage.
A motor controller controls and protects the operation of a motor. Its protective features are fuses, thermal overloads, and magnetic overloads.
Single-phase loads connect to a three-phase system phase-to-ground or phase-to-phase.
The 3-wire, single-phase Edison system is the only approved method of wiring single-phase power.
The 4-wire, three-phase Wye system is the safest possible multi-purpose distribution system for low voltage.
